linux.notes: One record covers all cores: RetroArch has a single retroarch.cfg, saves/, states/ and system/ shared by every core. Core-specific exceptions: (1) firmware names/subfolders in system/ are per core (docs.libretro.com library pages; lunchbox firmware_rules retroarch:* target the runtime system dir); (2) sort_savefiles_enable/sort_savestates_enable create per-core subdirectories named after the core's reported library_name; (3) cores control SRAM usage, so cores without SRAM never produce a .srm, and subsystem-based content (e.g. MAME softlists) uses subsystem-declared extensions; (4) savestate file naming has no frontend-level per-core variants - documented defaults are .state/.stateN/.state.auto for all cores (core docs such as Beetle PSX only note compatibility caveats, not different file names).

linux-flatpak.notes: Gap: the save/state/system defaults under ~/.var/app/org.libretro.RetroArch/config/retroarch/ are derived (Flatpak XDG redirection + RetroArch frontend defaults) rather than stated verbatim in flathub documentation; the controller guide does explicitly confirm the .var/app config path for autoconfig. The manifest grants --filesystem=host and --filesystem=/run/udev:ro, so content files and controller device access work from any host location.

windows.notes: Windows RetroArch is portable-first: the distributed layout is a single RetroArch install folder holding retroarch.cfg, saves\, states\, system\ and autoconfig\ together. macos.notes: macOS defaults split data: retroarch.cfg and autoconfig/ live under ~/Library/Application Support/RetroArch (config/ subdir for the main config), while saves/, states/ and system/ default to ~/Documents/RetroArch so users can find and sync them. Portable installs (portable.txt, RAPortableInstall, Steam) concentrate everything next to the .app bundle. Verified on master and v1.19.1; older builds that wrote retroarch.cfg directly under ~/Library/Application Support/RetroArch (without the config/ segment) were not separately pinned.
